do: Use semantic HTML elements to convey structure (h1-h6 for headings, ul/ol/dl for lists, table/th/td for tabular data)
Use HTML heading tags (h1–h6) to represent content hierarchy in a meaningful order
Associate form labels with controls using <label for='id'> or aria-labelledby
Group related form controls using <fieldset> and <legend> elements
Use proper table markup with <th> elements for headers and scope/headers attributes for complex tables
Use ARIA landmarks (main, navigation, banner, contentinfo) to identify page regions
Provide programmatic associations between related content using aria-describedby
Use semantic list markup (<ul>, <ol>, <dl>) for grouped related items
Associate table captions with tables using <caption> element
Use headings to create logical document structure and hierarchy
Group radio buttons and checkboxes with fieldset/legend when they share a common question
Use aria-labelledby to connect multiple text elements that describe a single control
Implement ARIA roles (button, link, heading) when semantic HTML isn't available
Use scope='row' or scope='col' to associate simple table headers with data cells
Provide table summaries for complex tables using aria-describedby referencing detailed description
Implement proper nesting of headings (don't skip levels: h1→h2→h3)
Use aria-required='true' to indicate required form fields programmatically
Group related sections with <section> elements and descriptive headings
Use role='group' with aria-labelledby for custom grouped controls when fieldset isn't suitable
Use ARIA roles and properties only when native HTML doesn’t convey the necessary relationships
dont: Do not rely on visual formatting alone (bold, italics, color) to convey structural meaning

Do not use
or   to create visual spacing that implies structure
Do not use tables for layout purposes (use CSS for visual layout)
Do not omit <label> elements or proper associations for form controls
Do not use <div> or <span> elements as headings without role='heading' and aria-level
Do not use placeholder text as the sole label for form inputs

Do not create fake lists using
or bullet characters without proper list markup
Do not use <th> elements in layout tables (F46 failure)
Do not insert meaningful content using CSS :before/:after pseudo-elements (F87 failure)
Do not use structural markup for purely presentational effects (F43 failure)
Do not fail to update id/headers associations in complex tables (F90 failure)
Do not use changes in text presentation alone to convey information (F2 failure)
Do not associate data cells with headers using id/headers incorrectly
Do not create visual hierarchies without corresponding semantic markup
Do not use font size or color alone to indicate headings
Do not omit fieldset/legend for radio button groups that share a question
Do not use title attribute alone as the primary labeling mechanism
Do not create custom controls without proper ARIA roles and properties
Do not use whitespace or positioning to indicate relationships between elements
Do not skip heading levels in document structure (h1 to h3 without h2)
Do not use visual styling (e.g., bold text, larger font, spacing) to imply structure without semantic markup
Do not use <div> or <span> in place of semantic elements unless ARIA roles are properly applied
Do not duplicate content visually and programmatically unless hidden from assistive tech
Do not use empty heading tags to create spacing — headings must convey meaning
Do not rely solely on placeholder text for labeling form controls
edge_cases: Complex data tables: Use id/headers attributes when scope isn't sufficient for multi-level headers
Dynamic content: Ensure programmatic relationships are maintained when content changes via JavaScript
Custom controls: Implement proper ARIA roles, states, and properties for non-standard widgets
Multi-part forms: Use fieldset/legend for each logical section with related controls
Error messages: Associate error text with form controls using aria-describedby
Progressive disclosure: Maintain semantic relationships when content is revealed/hidden
Date inputs: Group day/month/year fields with fieldset/legend for screen reader context
Address forms: Group street, city, state, zip fields under fieldset with 'Address' legend
Payment forms: Separate billing/shipping address sections with distinct fieldsets
Search forms: Use role='search' on form element containing search functionality
Data visualizations: Provide structured data alternatives (tables, lists) for charts and graphs
Card layouts: Use proper heading hierarchy within each card for scannable structure
Tabs interface: Implement proper ARIA tablist/tab/tabpanel relationships
Accordion widgets: Use proper button/region relationships with aria-controls and aria-expanded
Breadcrumb navigation: Use ordered list markup with proper link relationships
Multi-column layouts: Ensure reading order makes sense when CSS is disabled
Form validation: Associate validation messages with specific fields using aria-describedby
Required field indicators: Use aria-required='true' plus visual indicators
Table sorting: Update aria-sort attribute values when column sort changes
Nested lists: Properly structure sub-lists within parent list items
Definition terms: Use <dl><dt><dd> structure for glossaries and specification lists
Mathematical expressions: Use MathML or structured text alternatives
Code examples: Use <pre><code> with proper language identification
Survey forms: Group rating scale questions with fieldset/legend structure
Multiple navigation regions: use aria-label to differentiate (e.g., 'Primary navigation', 'Footer navigation')
Information presented visually as headings, tables, or groups is not represented programmatically in structure.
Elements rely on visual layout alone to convey hierarchy, not semantic or ARIA markup.
Form inputs that belong to a single question group are not programmatically linked together.
Improper use of structural elements like lists or tables breaks expected relationships.
Automation tools often confirm presence of markup but not correctness of logical hierarchy.
Improper heading implementation using spans with CSS styling instead of semantic HTML.
Complex heading structures broken across multiple elements with line breaks.
Semantic meaning preservation when headings are styled rather than marked up properly.

H51: Using table markup to present tabular information

H49: Using semantic markup to mark emphasized or special text
G115: Using semantic elements to mark up structure
ARIA11: Using ARIA landmarks to identify regions of a page
ARIA13: Using aria-labelledby to name regions and landmarks
ARIA16: Using aria-labelledby to provide a name for user interface controls
ARIA17: Using grouping roles to identify related form controls
ARIA20: Using the region role to identify a region of the page
H39: Using caption elements to associate data table captions with data tables
H63: Using the scope attribute to associate header cells with data cells
H43: Using id and headers attributes to associate data cells with header cells in data tables
G117: Using text to convey information that is conveyed by variations in presentation of text
G140: Separating information and structure from presentation to enable different presentations
H48: Using ol, ul, and dl for lists or groups of links
H85: Using fieldset and legend elements to group form controls
ARIA9: Using aria-labelledby to associate text with controls
ARIA10: Using aria-describedby to provide descriptive information
axe_rules_hint: landmark-one-main: Ensures only one main landmark exists
region: Ensures all page content is contained by landmarks
list: Ensures <ul>, <ol> and <dl> elements are structured correctly
listitem: Ensures <li> elements are used semantically
definition-list: Ensures <dl> elements are structured correctly
dlitem: Ensures <dt> and <dd> elements are used correctly
th-has-data-cells: Ensures table headers have data cells they describe
td-headers-attr: Ensures table data cells use headers attribute correctly
table-fake-caption: Ensures fake table captions are not used
scope-attr-valid: Ensures scope attribute is used correctly on tables
label: Ensures every form element has an associated label
fieldset: Ensures fieldsets have legend elements
heading-order: Ensures heading elements follow a logical, sequential order
form-field-multiple-labels: Ensures form fields are not associated with multiple labels incorrectly
